First, we note that

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -\infty }-\frac{{x}^{5}}{4} & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }(-\frac{1}{4}\cdot {x}^{5}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}\cdot {lim}_{x\to -\infty }{x}^{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

The graph $y={x}^{5}$ is power function with an odd positive power and therefore has the property that

$$
{lim}_{x\to -\infty }{x}^{5}=-\infty .
$$

Multiplication by the negative constant $-\frac{1}{4}$ changes the sign of the limit. 
So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{4}\cdot {lim}_{x\to -\infty }{x}^{5} & =-{lim}_{x\to -\infty }{x}^{5}=\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
{lim}_{x\to -\infty }(-\frac{{x}^{5}}{4})=\infty .
$$
